src/application/usecases/UpdateOrderStatusUseCase.ts: `const validStatuses: OrderStatus[] = ['placed', 'paid', 'packed', 'shipped', 'delivered'];` hard-codes the status list before `order.transitionTo(newStatus)`

parsedVerdict.reasoning:
Most of the module is cohesive. Each order and stock use case gets persistence through the injected domain repositories (OrderRepository, ProductRepository) and no use case calls a database or ORM directly. Two things break that consistency.

1. ListOrdersByStatusUseCase is a read-only query, but it also has a method `validateExecute(request: CreateOrderRequest)`. That method imports `assertExecuteRule` from PlaceOrderUseCase.ts, which is the place-order rule that an order must have at least one line. So a write-side validation for a different use case sits inside a query class. It is a call to one shared definition, not a copy, so it is not duplication. It does split the file into two unrelated concerns. It also means PlaceOrderUseCase.ts exports its own validation rule as a free function for other use cases to import, so that file is no longer only a use case.

2. Every use case writes out the same Order-to-OrderDto mapping (id, status, lines, createdAt.toISOString()). PlaceOrderUseCase has it as the private `mapToDto`, and the other three repeat it inline instead of sharing one mapping. Also, UpdateOrderStatusUseCase hard-codes `validStatuses: OrderStatus[] = ['placed','paid','packed','shipped','delivered']` before calling `order.transitionTo`. This probably restates the status list and transition rule that the Order entity defines. Order.ts is not in the material, so I can't confirm that one.

The main finding is the misplaced validation in ListOrdersByStatusUseCase together with the rule exported from PlaceOrderUseCase. The repeated mapping and the status list are supporting evidence.

violations.message: The query use case ListOrdersByStatusUseCase has `validateExecute(request: CreateOrderRequest)`, which calls PlaceOrderUseCase's `assertExecuteRule`. This puts a place-order validation, an unrelated write-side concern, into a list-by-status use case.

`export function assertExecuteRule` exposes PlaceOrderUseCase's own request rule as a free function that other use cases import. The rule leaves its use case's boundary instead of living in one dedicated validation place.

Hard-codes `validStatuses: OrderStatus[] = ['placed','paid','packed','shipped','delivered']` before calling `order.transitionTo`. This probably copies the status list and transition rule from the Order domain type instead of relying on the entity. It also repeats the inline Order->OrderDto mapping.
